pages.title: AgentSam documentation
pages.summary: Understand the SDK, its execution environments, and how to verify an agent workflow before relying on it.

content.heading: Start with a verified environment
content.body: Confirm the installed AgentSam SDK version, choose an authorized execution environment, and verify your account's available tools before running a cookbook. Documentation examples describe intended behavior; verify CLI availability against the installed release.

content.heading: Explore the documentation
content.description: Choose a focused guide or a runnable verification workflow.

pages.title: AgentSam cookbooks
pages.summary: Task-oriented engineering recipes with prerequisites, examples, expected results, and failure checks.

content.heading: Use a recipe to prove an outcome
content.body: Each cookbook is a repeatable test, not a list of unexplained commands. Start with a clean repository or isolated workspace, record your baseline, and compare observed behavior with the expected result. Treat undocumented or unavailable CLI flags as a verification failure, not a reason to invent substitute commands.

content.heading: Infrastructure recipes
content.description: The first independently editable cookbook pages migrated from the original field manual.

content.title: Publication rule
content.body: Code examples in this migration are source-preserving drafts. Their runtime support must be checked against the current released SDK before any cookbook is marked runnable.

pages.title: Detect changes with Merkle snapshots
pages.summary: Compare two repository snapshots and determine which work can be reused after a bounded change.

content.heading: What you'll verify
content.body: Given one small, controlled repository change, the system should identify the affected subtree and distinguish reusable prior analysis from work that needs to be recomputed. Prerequisites: a repository you can inspect, a saved baseline, and an AgentSam CLI release with the documented Merkle operations.

content.heading: Make one bounded change
content.body: Change exactly one tracked source file in an isolated working copy. Record the edited path and avoid changing dependencies or generated output at the same time. Capture a second snapshot and compare the two states.

content.label: Comparison — original cookbook example
content.code:
agentsam merkle snapshot . --semantic --out /tmp/sam-after.json
agentsam merkle diff /tmp/sam-before.json /tmp/sam-after.json --json

content.title: Expected result
content.body: The comparison identifies changed subtrees and produces evidence for invalidated versus reusable analysis. If the installed CLI cannot execute these flags, record the mismatch as a documentation issue and do not mark this recipe verified.

pages.title: Compare local and remote terminals
pages.summary: Confirm that two authorized execution lanes report consistent repository identity and environment evidence.

content.heading: Capture a read-only baseline
content.body: Run the same read-only probe through two authorized terminals. Record the host, current directory, repository commit, and Node.js version. Differences are evidence that the environments are not equivalent, not an invitation to silently rewrite configuration.

content.title: Expected result
content.body: Both executions return a consistent repository revision when intentionally pointed at the same checkout. Host and working-directory differences must be reported rather than hidden. No write operation is needed to perform this comparison.

pages.title: Native runtime and execution environments
pages.summary: Understand what belongs on the local machine, in the hosted control plane, and in an isolated execution environment.

content.heading: Separate control and execution
content.body: Account authorization and execution placement are different responsibilities. A user request must resolve to a permitted connection and environment before a terminal job starts. The runtime should report its host, execution lane, working directory, and completion status.

content.heading: Local and hosted behavior
content.body: Local development can operate against a registered device. Hosted execution requires an explicitly available service or sandbox. Documentation must distinguish supported behavior from proposed capabilities and verify the current release before claiming parity.

pages.title: Structured decisions
pages.summary: Make routing, confidence, approval, and action selection explicit in agent workflows.

content.heading: Decisions are inspectable
content.body: An agent should be able to explain which alternatives were considered, what evidence was available, and why a particular tool or execution lane was selected. The decision record is distinct from the model's prose response.

content.heading: Gates, scores, and confidence
content.body: A gate determines whether an action is permitted. A score helps compare allowed alternatives. Confidence expresses uncertainty and should not bypass the approval boundary. A useful trace records all three without presenting a guess as verified execution.
